learning_outcomes.text: Understand the concepts of rigid body kinematics and know the expressions for calculating velocities and accelerations in different types of motion. Apply this knowledge to obtain them in various cases.

Define the concepts of center of mass and moments and products of inertia, and know Steiner's theorems relating them. Solve problems calculating them. Understand the influence of a body's mass distribution on its motion.
Solve situations of rigid body and mixed body equilibrium.

State the general laws of dynamics and derived theorems, understanding the conditions for their use, and apply them to problem-solving, evaluating different methods and justifying the choice of each one.
Understand the concept of percussive force and its importance. Solve exercises.
Acquire skills related to laboratory work in Advanced Mechanics, and with the treatment of measurements and errors.
Draft reports on experimental practices carried out in the Advanced Mechanics laboratory, including error treatment.

syllabus_topics: Dynamics of the rigid body: general equations of motion
Dynamics of the rigid body: energetic theorems
Static and dynamic balancing of a rotating system
Gyroscope: Stability and stable precessional motion
teaching_methods: Presentation and defense of problems, assignments, projects
Use of experimental data processing software
Analysis of results and preparation of practice reports
Evaluation activities in very small groups
Coordination and monitoring activities in very small groups

assessment_methods.method: Theory and Problem Evaluation (continuous assessment + final exam)
Laboratory Evaluation (continuous assessment and/or final exam)

assessment_rules: The Theory and Problem (TP) evaluation is calculated as 0.1*Deliveries + 0.9*Final Exam, requiring a minimum of 4 in the final exam. The Laboratory (CL) evaluation requires a minimum of 4 in continuous assessment or the final lab exam. The final grade (Cf) is Cf = 0.8*TP + 0.2*CL. If minimum limits are not met, the final grade will be the final exam grade. If the final exam grade is above 5 but the lab part is failed, the final grade will be 4. Both parts must be passed in the same call; grades are not carried over to subsequent calls within the same academic year.
